title: Virtual Networks and Subnets
description: Learn how Azure virtual networks provide isolated network environments and how subnets organize resources inside them.

data.text: An Azure Virtual Network, or VNet, is your own private network in the Azure cloud. Think of it like a corporate office network, but hosted in Azure. You decide which resources can talk to each other, how they connect to the internet, and whether they can reach your on-premises data center.

A VNet is a logically isolated section of the Azure network dedicated to your subscription. Every VNet has its own private IP address range defined by you. Resources inside a VNet can communicate securely with each other by default.

data.title: Key VNet properties
items: **Address space**: A range of private IP addresses you define, like 10.0.0.0/16
**Subnets**: Segments inside the VNet that group resources by role or tier
**DNS servers**: Custom DNS if you need to resolve internal names
**Service endpoints**: Secure direct connections to Azure services like storage

data.text: A subnet is a smaller range of IP addresses carved out of your VNet's address space. You might have a frontend subnet for web servers, a backend subnet for application servers, and a data subnet for databases. This makes security and routing easier because you can apply rules to entire groups of resources.

data.title: Create a VNet with two subnets using Azure CLI
data.content: Azure CLI to create a VNet and subnets
data.code:
az network vnet create \
  --name MyVNet \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name FrontendSubnet \
  --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24

az network vnet subnet create \
  --vnet-name MyVNet \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name BackendSubnet \
  --address-prefix 10.0.2.0/24

data.text: VNet peering connects two virtual networks together so resources in either VNet can talk to each other as if they were in the same network. Peering can be within the same region or across regions, and it is also possible to peer across different Azure subscriptions.

terms.definition: An isolated network in Azure that you fully control.
A smaller IP range within a VNet used to group and secure resources.
A connection between two VNets so resources can communicate privately.
The CIDR range you assign to a VNet, like 10.0.0.0/16.

data.title: Create Your First VNet
data.description: Use Azure CLI or the Azure portal to create a VNet with at least two subnets.
steps: Create a VNet with an address prefix like 10.0.0.0/16
Verify the subnets appear in the Azure portal
data.expectedOutcome: A VNet with two subnets is visible in the Azure portal.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: A VNet is an isolated private network in Azure.
Subnets segment a VNet for security and organization.
VNet peering connects separate VNets privately.
You define address spaces using CIDR notation.
data.takeaway: VNets and subnets are the foundation of Azure networking.
